responses:
**Summary of Search Results:**

1. **Loss Runs (AUTO-2024-001, 3yr):** 3 claims over 3 years — two 2023 physical damage claims (closed, $14,200 total), one 2024 bodily injury claim (open, $85,000 reserve, litigation flagged 11/2/24, reserve strengthened twice, most recently 3/14/25). No 2025 claims. Trailing 3-year loss ratio: 0.61 on $163,400 written premium.

2. **NJ Regulatory Bulletins (Commercial Auto, post-1/1/25):** Three bulletins — (25-04) revised UM/UIM forms due by 1/1/26; (25-11) telematics surcharges must be disclosed at quote (not bind) and reversible within 30 days; (25-19) non-payment cancellation grace period extended from 10 to 15 days for policies over $25,000 premium.

3. **Internal KB – VIN Validation Failures:** Null VINs occur from checksum failures (common with faxed ACORD 127s confusing "0"/"O"). VINs should never be inferred from make/model — route to human review. A null VIN blocks rating but not quoting, if underwriter accepts the flag.

4. **Filed Rates (Meridian, NY, 2026):** Base rates by radius: $2,140 (<50mi), $2,890 (50-200mi), $3,410 (200-300mi). Fleet credits: 5%/9%/12% at 10/20/30 units. Telematics credit up to 15%. Surcharges: 22% (driver <23), 40% (major violation in trailing 36 months).

5. **Claim Notes (HOME-2024-003):** Address discrepancy identified between loss location and declarations (unit number mismatch), attributed by insured to application typo. Underwriting requested corrected ACORD 80; still outstanding as of 3/30/25, task reassigned. No coverage decision made.

6. **Competitor Filings (Commercial Auto, PA, post-6/1/25):** Keystone Casualty filed 6.4% rate increase (effective 2/1/26), targeting 200-300 mile radius bands. Allegheny Indemnity introduced a telematics program (up to 20% credit, plus 5% first-term participation credit). No eligibility rule changes from either filer.

7. **Reinsurance Treaty Terms (2026, Commercial Auto):** Quota share retention raised to $500,000/occurrence (from $350,000). Aggregate stop loss attaches at 78% loss ratio. Risks with radius >300 miles are excluded from treaty — making radius a treaty compliance issue, not just an appetite consideration. Cession statements due within 45 days of quarter-end.
